profile.headline: Software Engineer at Microsoft
profile.summary:
Working as a Software Developer at Edaptive Computing Inc, I've been able to get first-hand experience with the process of designing software and implementing it in accordance to client requirements. I've come to really enjoy class design and the satisfaction of seeing things work as planned, and to really appreciate careful documentation. 

I've acquired substantial experience with both backend and frontend development, but primarily the backend; I've also spent time as both a Scrum Master and Tech Lead, and been heavily involved with the organization and coordination with my team members, helping to make sure that our Agile process can meet the client's deadlines.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description: I have been working under Professor Stephen Fitzgerald, studying Metal-Organic Frameworks and creating statistical simulations of Hydrogen/HD/Deuterium molecules interacting with those MOFs.

positions.title: Stacks Worker at Mudd Library
positions.description: I've worked in Mudd Library, sorting and shelving books, as well as handling check-ins and troubleshooting anomalies using the computer database.

projects.title: Creating a Pokemon-Showdown AI using Machine Learning
projects.description: Sam and I chose for our final project in Machine Learning & Data Mining to create a bot which uses the Markov-Decision Process to determine its optimal actions.

projects.title: Summer Research statistical simulation
projects.description: Simulate Hydrogen molecules attaching to a sample of MOF-5 over time, with temperature as a variable. This project was done over August, 2016, while working in Professor Stephen Fitzgerald's lab. The goal was to write a program which could statistically model hydrogen gas molecules sticking to a sample of MOF-5, and examining the effect of temperature and concentrations on the proportion of gas molecules which stuck.

testScores.name: SAT
testScores.description: I received a 620 on the Writing section, 710 on the Reading section, and 720 on the Math section.
